To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ViSOR framework can: (i) be used to annotate, retrieve, share and download surveillance videos, (ii) be used to evaluate the performance of automatic systems, (iii) be used to compare the annotations of different users and/or systems, and (iv) be used to collect new surveillance data.

the proposed ViSOR framework allows to (i) integrate the video surveillance domain with other multimedia applications; (ii) exploit both ontology-based and content-based retrieval; (iii) support both automatic and manual annotation; (iv) support both the annotation and retrieval of multimedia data; and (v) support the evaluation of the performance of surveillance systems.

1) the ViSOR platform is a useful tool for collecting and managing surveillance videos; 2) the ViSOR ontology is a useful tool to annotate videos and to perform retrieval; 3) the ViSOR evaluation desk is a useful tool that allows to evaluate the quality of the annotation and the retrieval performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the definition of a novel framework for video surveillance, which is aimed to provide an open platform for video sharing, annotation and evaluation.
providing a flexible and open platform which can be used by the community to share and evaluate surveillance videos and annotations.

developing an integrated framework which is able to provide a common platform for the research community, allowing the sharing of surveillance data, the comparison of different annotations and the performance evaluation of video analysis systems.
